title: CORS: "same origin" is derived from the request's own Host header with no list of expected host names, so a DNS-rebinding page passes the CORS gate and can read /health and send unlimited login guesses from the operator's browser

evidence.note: per-request cors(): Origin absent -> allow (:122); Origin whose URL.origin equals scheme://<request Host header> -> allow (:101, :113, :126); allowlist (:133); otherwise 403 (:138-140)

evidence.ref: node cors-host.js <snapshot>/src/api/server.ts <repo>/node_modules (scratch folder outside the repo (Node 22.16.0 by absolute path; no src/ import, no .env, no data/, no live DB; loopback 127.0.0.1 only; audit-base snapshot from slice-files.ts --snapshot API,DASH); the exact text of server.ts:97-144 transpiled with the repo typescript and mounted in a bare express 5.2.1 app with cors 2.8.6, empty env = shipped defaults)
evidence.note: output: Host=evil.example:8080 + Origin=http://evil.example:8080 -> 200 {"reachedRoute":true}; Host=127.0.0.1:8080 + Origin=http://evil.example:8080 -> 403; Host=127.0.0.1:8080 + Origin=http://127.0.0.1:3000 -> 403; no Origin -> 200
/health and /api/auth/login are mounted before authMiddleware (no session needed)
loginHandler: no attempt counter, delay or lockout; a failure only logs warn (:56)
a correct key sets the session cookie for whatever host the browser used, so a rebinding hostname gets its own valid session, which then passes authMiddleware (:101-110) for every control route
the dev proxy forwards without changeOrigin, so Host stays localhost:5173 and the same Host-match lets dev requests through; any Host allowlist must keep this working
default bind 127.0.0.1; 0.0.0.0 documented for remote access

sibling_sites_checked: Every request-origin decision in src/api: server.ts:97-144 (HTTP, this finding); ws/handler.ts:37-66 (WebSocket upgrade, no Origin check at all, AUD-API-006); no Host allowlist anywhere (grep 'host' over the snapshot: server.ts:101/:113/:208, handler.ts:43). Express trust proxy is off and X-Forwarded-Proto is honoured only with DASHBOARD_TRUST_PROXY_PROTO=1 (server.ts:99, :105-108), correct. A rebinding hostname does not receive the existing 127.0.0.1/localhost session cookie, so an already logged-in operator session is not reused (mitigating). Login without rate limit is also listed under authentication handling (AUD-API-007); /health content is AUD-API-010.
severity_rationale: S2 EXPOSURE: the trust boundary (only the dashboard itself may drive the API from a browser) can be crossed by any web page the operator visits while the bot runs, without network access to the bot: the page reads /health (positions, exposure, 24 h P&L) and can guess the key at browser speed with no limit. Taking control (emergency-sell, resume, chain stop, CB reset) needs a correct key; preflight refuses keys shorter than 16 characters (docs/operations/going-live.md:147), so a random key makes that impractical, while a human-chosen 16-character phrase may not. Not S1 because control needs the key; the code half is proven on loopback, the browser half (rebinding) is not run here.
recommendation: Check the Host header against an allowlist (DASHBOARD_HOST:PORT, 127.0.0.1/localhost/[::1] on the configured port, any configured public name, the vite dev host) before CORS and reject others (421/403), and derive "same origin" from that configured list rather than from Host; add login rate limiting with backoff. Card API-03 (it changes which requests are accepted). Phase 29 unless the dashboard is exposed beyond 127.0.0.1 earlier.

sub_claims.claim: Any request whose Origin equals its own Host passes the CORS gate; there is no host allowlist
evidence: node cors-host.js (loopback repro, output in evidence)

sub_claims.claim: A DNS-rebinding page can therefore read /health and POST login guesses without limit from the operator's browser
A correct guess yields a session for the rebinding hostname that passes authMiddleware on every control route
